- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: ShareOnboardingGuide
tools.description:
Upload the ONBOARDING.md in the current directory and return a share link teammates can open in Claude Code. Call this after the user has confirmed the final content.

When called with the default mode='check': if a local ONBOARDING.md is present, uploads it to the most-recently-updated org guide (or creates one if none exist) and returns a fresh link. If no local file is present, returns the existing link without uploading (status: has_existing).

mode.description: 'check' (default): if ONBOARDING.md is present locally, uploads it to the most-recent guide (creates one if none exist); otherwise reports the existing link without uploading. 'update': upload to a specific guide by short_code. 'create': always make a new link. 'delete': remove the guide named by short_code; with no short_code, nothing is deleted and the user's guides are listed.

short_code.description: Short code of one guide, from an earlier call's result. Required by delete. With check or update, targets that guide instead of the most recently updated one.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

content.description: The content to write to the file

lastPrompt: 回答这四个自测题

content.text:
## 1. 为什么只命中 992 而不是 1000？

1000 ÷ 16 = 62.5，所以 system prompt 只填满了 62 个 block，即 992 个 token。

第 63 个 block 装的是 system prompt 的最后 8 个 token 加上用户问题的前 8 个 token。哈希是对整块 16 个 token 算的，两个请求的用户问题不同，这一块的哈希就不同，无法命中。

所以 system prompt 的最后 8 个 token 要和用户问题一起重算，实际 prefill 的是 8 + 50 = 58 个 token。

## 2. block 在空闲队列里又能被命中，为什么不冲突？

因为"空闲"只表示引用计数为零、当前没人在用，显存里的数据并没有被擦掉，哈希表里的条目也还在。

之后有两种结局，谁先发生算谁的：
- **先被命中**：从空闲队列里摘出来，引用计数变为 1，重新成为在用的 block。
- **先被分配给新请求**：这时才从哈希表里删除条目，内容随后被覆盖。

调度器是单线程逐步执行的，这两个动作不会同时发生，所以没有竞争。

## 3. 抢占一个已生成 500 token 的请求，代价是什么？

**恢复代价**：把 prompt 加上已生成的 500 个 token 重新 prefill 一遍，再加上回到等待队列的排队时间。

这比看上去便宜：那 500 个 token 当初是 500 步逐个生成的，重算时作为输入并行处理，一步或几步（受 token 预算切块）就能算完。如果它释放的满 block 还没被淘汰，还能命中自己留下的前缀缓存，重算量更少。

**为什么选重算而不是换出**：这里要修正我上一轮的说法，"传输不比重算快多少"说得偏强。单看速度，把几百 MB 的 KV 经 PCIe 来回搬一趟未必比重算慢。更站得住的理由是：
- **简单**：换出要多维护一套 CPU 侧的 KV 存储和锁页内存，重算只需把"已算 token 数"清零。
- **抢占本应罕见**：它是超卖撑爆时的安全阀，为罕见路径做复杂优化不划算。
- **前缀缓存已经覆盖了大部分收益**：没被淘汰的 block 直接命中，相当于免费的"换入"。

## 4. 预算 512，12 个 decode 请求，1500 token 的新 prompt，几步出首 token？

**3 步。**

- 每步先给 12 个 decode 请求各 1 个 token，剩余预算 512 − 12 = 500。
- 新请求每步算 500 个 token：第 1 步算到 500，第 2 步算到 1000，第 3 步算到 1500。
- 第 3 步算完了 prompt 的最后一个 token，它的输出就用来采样首 token。

前提是没有前缀命中，且并发数没超过 `max_num_seqs`。即使期间有 decode 请求结束、腾出一点预算，每步最多也只有 512，1500 个 token 仍然需要 3 步。
继续详细讲解剩余概念

content.text:
剩下的是 SGLang 的三个核心概念（7–9），以及四个只需概念级掌握的进阶主题。

## 概念 7：RadixAttention

**目标和 vLLM 的 prefix caching 相同**：跨请求复用相同前缀的 KV。不同的是数据结构：vLLM 用"块哈希 → block"的平铺哈希表，SGLang 用一棵 radix tree。

**Radix tree 是什么**：压缩的前缀树。每条边是一段 token 序列（长度可变），每个节点保存这段 token 对应的 KV 位置。从根走到某个节点，路径上的 token 拼起来就是一个被缓存的前缀。

```
根
└─ [system prompt, 1000 token]
   ├─ [用户 A 第 1 轮问答] ── [用户 A 第 2 轮问答]
   └─ [用户 B 第 1 轮问答]
```

SGLang 的 KV 池是 **token 粒度**的：每个 token 一个槽位，节点里存的是一串槽位下标。

**三个操作**（对应 `radix_cache.py` 里的三个函数）

1. **匹配前缀**：拿新请求的 token 序列从根往下走，逐段比较。如果在某个节点的中间分叉，就把这个节点**拆成两个**，前半段成为公共父节点。返回命中的 KV 槽位，剩余 token 才需要 prefill。
2. **插入**：请求算完后，把它的完整序列（prompt 加输出）插进树里。输出也被缓存，所以多轮对话的下一轮能命中整个历史。
3. **淘汰**：显存不够时，按最近访问时间淘汰**叶子节点**。只能从叶子淘汰，因为子节点的 KV 依赖父节点的前缀，先删父节点会让子树全部失效。叶子删掉后，父节点若没有其他孩子，就成为新的叶子。

**引用计数**：正在运行的请求会给它路径上的所有节点加锁，被锁的节点不能淘汰。淘汰同样是惰性的：缓存占着本来空闲的槽位，要用时才腾。

**面试答法（和 vLLM 块哈希的差别）**

| | vLLM | SGLang |
|---|---|---|
| 数据结构 | 平铺哈希表 | radix tree |
| 粒度 | 16 token 的满 block | 单个 token |
| 命中长度 | 向下取整到 16 的倍数 | 精确到 token |
| 淘汰顺序 | 空闲队列，释放时逆序入队来近似"先淘汰尾部" | 天然从叶子淘汰 |
| 前缀之间的关系 | 隐含在链式哈希里，看不见 | 树结构显式表达，调度器可以直接利用 |

粒度带来的差别其实很小，每个请求最多多算 15 个 token。真正的差别在最后一行：树让调度器能便宜地知道"每个等待请求能命中多长"，这是概念 8 的前提。

## 概念 8：Cache-aware 调度

**FCFS 的问题**：假设缓存只装得下一个长前缀，请求按 A1、B1、A2、B2 的顺序到达（A、B 是两组不同的前缀）。

- FCFS：A1 算完缓存了 A；B1 进来把 A 挤掉；A2 进来又把 B 挤掉。每个请求都重新 prefill，缓存来回抖动，命中率为零。
- 按前缀分组：A1、A2、B1、B2。A2 和 B2 都命中，prefill 量减半。

**做法：最长前缀匹配优先**。每轮调度时，对等待队列里的每个请求查一次树，得到命中长度，按命中长度从长到短排序后依次放行。和当前缓存最"亲近"的请求先跑，缓存被充分利用后才换下一组。

论文证明了：在离线场景下，按 radix tree 的深度优先顺序处理请求能达到最优命中率，而最长前缀匹配优先等价于这个顺序。

**工程上的几个处理**
- **退化为 FCFS**：等待队列很长时，逐个查树的开销太大，直接回到先来先服务。
- **批内去重**：几个等待请求共享同一个尚未缓存的前缀时，先放行一个，其余稍后再进，这样后面的都能命中，避免同一个前缀被重复计算。
- **代价是公平性**：命中短的请求可能被反复插队，延迟变差。

**显存预算的差别**：vLLM 进场时只为 prompt 分配，撑爆了再抢占。据我了解，SGLang 放行新请求时会按输出上限预估并预留一部分空间，更保守，抢占更少；预留不够时也有类似的回退机制，把部分 decode 请求撤回队列。

**面试答法**：缓存命中率不只取决于缓存结构，还取决于请求的执行顺序。cache-aware 调度是用一点公平性换命中率，在前缀高度共享的负载（agent、few-shot、多轮对话）下收益最大，前缀互不相同时没有收益。

## 概念 9：结构化输出

**目标**：保证输出一定符合给定的 JSON schema、正则或语法，而不是靠提示词"希望"它符合。

**基本机制：约束解码**
1. 把约束编译成自动机：正则编译成有限状态机；JSON schema 这类有嵌套的结构需要带栈的自动机。
2. 每一步 decode：根据自动机当前状态，算出词表里哪些 token 合法，生成一个掩码。
3. 把不合法 token 的 logits 设为负无穷，再采样。
4. 用采到的 token 推进自动机状态。

**难点：token 不等于字符**。自动机按字符定义，而一个 token 可能跨多个字符，词表有十几万个 token。每步逐个检查太慢，所以要预计算"状态 → 合法 token 集合"的索引，运行时只查表。带栈的语法没法完全预计算，做法是把 token 分成两类：合法性与栈无关的预计算，与栈有关的少数 token 运行时再查。

**掩码的开销在哪**：它是 CPU 上的工作，每个请求每一步都要做，而且卡在两次 GPU 前向之间。batch 大时可能成为瓶颈，所以实现上会让掩码计算和 GPU 前向并行进行。

**Jump-forward**：JSON 里很多内容是确定的。比如 schema 规定下一个字段是 `"name"`，那么 `{"name": "` 这一串只有一种合法走法，没必要让模型一个 token 一个 token 地生成。

- 做法：把自动机里只有唯一出路的连续状态压缩成一条边，走到这里时直接把整段文本追加到序列里。
- 追加的 token 作为输入处理，相当于一小段 prefill，一步算完，省掉了多步 decode。
- 是否启用取决于所用的语法后端和版本。

**面试答法**
- 为什么约束解码可能比自由生成更快：确定性片段被跳过，decode 步数减少。
- 局限：只保证语法合法，不保证内容正确；强行屏蔽模型原本想输出的 token 会改变分布，可能降低内容质量。

## 进阶主题（概念级）

每个只需讲清"解决什么、怎么做、代价是什么"。

**量化**
- 解决：权重太大，占显存，且 decode 受带宽限制，读得越多越慢。
- 做法：把 fp16 权重压成 8 位或 4 位。AWQ、GPTQ 是用少量校准数据挑选量化值、减小精度损失的方法；KV Cache 也可以量化来扩大容量。
- 代价：精度下降，位数越低越明显。

**投机解码**
- 解决：decode 一步只出一个 token。
- 做法：小模型先猜 k 个 token，大模型一次前向并行验证，接受最长的正确前缀。配合特定的接受规则，输出分布与原模型一致。
- 为什么成立：回到概念 1，带宽受限时验证 k 个 token 的耗时和生成 1 个差不多。
- 代价：收益取决于接受率；高负载下 batch 已经把算力用满，多出的验证计算反而拖慢整体。

**多卡并行**
- Tensor parallel：把每层的权重矩阵切到多张卡上，每层算完做一次汇总。能装下单卡放不下的模型并降低延迟，代价是每层都有通信，依赖高速互联。
- Pipeline parallel：按层切，前几层在卡 1，后几层在卡 2。通信少，但单请求延迟不降。

**Prefill/decode 分离**
- 解决：概念 6 里 prefill 和 decode 互相干扰的根本问题。
- 做法：prefill 和 decode 放在不同实例上，prefill 算完把 KV 传给 decode 实例。两边可以各自调参、各自扩缩容。
- 代价：KV 要跨机器传输，系统复杂度上升。

## 两个框架的总对比

| | vLLM | SGLang |
|---|---|---|
| KV 管理 | 分页，block 为 16 token | token 粒度的槽位池 |
| 前缀缓存 | 块的链式哈希 + 哈希表 | radix tree |
| 淘汰 | 空闲队列的 LRU | 叶子节点的 LRU |
| 调度顺序 | FCFS 或优先级 | 默认最长前缀匹配优先 |
| 显存不足时 | 超卖，抢占后重算 | 预留输出空间，必要时撤回 |
| 强项 | 生态和通用性，文档多 | 前缀高度共享的负载、结构化输出 |

1. 淘汰为什么只能从叶子节点开始？
2. 新请求的前缀在某个节点的中间位置分叉，树会怎么变？

4. 为什么投机解码在低负载时有效，高负载时可能适得其反？
5. 约束解码保证了什么，不保证什么？

content.text:
## 1. 淘汰为什么只能从叶子节点开始？

因为子节点的 KV 依赖它前面的全部前缀。一个节点保存的只是"它这一段 token"的 KV，这些值是在前缀已知的条件下算出来的，单独拿出来没有意义。

如果先删中间节点，它下面的子树虽然还占着显存，但再也无法被匹配到（匹配必须从根连续走下来），等于白占空间。从叶子删则不影响任何其他节点。叶子删掉后，父节点如果没有别的孩子，就变成新的叶子，成为下一轮的候选。

## 2. 新请求在某个节点的中间位置分叉，树会怎么变？

那个节点被**拆成两个**。

假设节点存着 100 个 token，新请求只和它的前 60 个相同：
- 前 60 个 token 成为一个新的父节点，带走对应的 60 个 KV 槽位；
- 后 40 个 token 留在原节点里，变成这个父节点的孩子；
- 新请求命中这 60 个 token，它剩余的部分算完后，作为父节点的另一个孩子插入。

拆分只改树的结构和槽位下标的归属，不复制也不重算任何 KV。

## 3. Cache-aware 调度收益最小和最大的负载

**没有收益**：每个请求的前缀互不相同，比如没有 system prompt 的单轮独立问答。所有请求的命中长度都是零，排序没有意义，结果等同于 FCFS。另一种情况是缓存足够大、装得下所有前缀，这时任何顺序都能命中，调度顺序也无关紧要。

**收益最大**：前缀分成若干组、组内高度共享、且缓存装不下所有组。典型例子：
- 多个 agent 各带不同的长 system prompt 和工具定义，请求交错到达；
- few-shot 评测，不同任务各有一长串示例；
- 很多用户的长多轮对话并发进行。

这时 FCFS 会让各组前缀互相挤掉，而按最长前缀优先能把同组请求集中处理。

## 4. 为什么投机解码在低负载有效、高负载可能适得其反？

**低负载**：batch 小，decode 处在带宽受限区间，算力大量闲置。大模型一次前向验证 k 个 token，耗时和生成 1 个差不多，相当于用闲置算力换来一步多出几个 token。

**高负载**：batch 已经很大，算力被用满，进入算力受限区间。这时：
- 每个请求每步要验证 k 个 token 而不是 1 个，步内 token 总数乘以 k，每步耗时明显变长；
- 被拒绝的那些 token 的计算全部浪费；
- 小模型本身还要占一份算力和显存。

所以高负载下总吞吐可能反而下降。它和 batching 争的是同一份闲置算力，batching 已经用掉了，投机解码就没有可用的了。

## 5. 约束解码保证了什么，不保证什么？

**保证**：输出在语法上一定合法。比如一定是能解析的 JSON，字段名和类型一定符合 schema，一定匹配给定的正则。

**不保证**：
- **内容正确**：字段里的值可能是错的或编造的，约束只管形式。
- **质量不受影响**：屏蔽掉模型原本想输出的 token 后，模型被迫走概率较低的路径，后续内容可能变差。
- **完整性**：如果在结构闭合前就达到了输出长度上限，得到的仍是被截断的不合法输出。

这九个概念到此讲完。按之前的安排，下一步是读源码：先读 vLLM 的 `scheduler.py`，目标是能画出一个请求从到达到返回的完整路径。

message.content: 自测题2 ：后 40 个 token 留在原节点里，变成这个父节点的孩子； 应该说原节点拆分出一个长40的子节点，新请求从第61个token开始到结尾形成一个新节点，这样理解对吗？

content.text:
对，结果的树结构就是你说的这样：一个长 60 的父节点，下面两个孩子，一个是原来的后 40 个 token，一个是新请求从分叉点到结尾的部分。

两个细节补充：

**1. 哪个是"新建的"节点，实现上和你的说法相反，但结构等价。**

SGLang 的拆分函数里，新建的是**前 60 个 token 的父节点**，原节点对象保留后 40 个，并改挂到新父节点下面。

这样做的原因是：原节点如果已经有孩子，这些孩子接在后 40 个 token 之后，本来就该跟着后半段走。让原节点对象保留后半段，它的孩子就不用动。

**2. 新请求的节点不是匹配时立刻生成的。**

- 匹配时：只做拆分，返回命中的 60 个 token 的 KV 槽位。
- 算完后：新请求的剩余部分才作为新节点插入，成为父节点的第二个孩子。

另外，"第 61 个 token"是相对这个节点的起点说的。如果这个节点前面还有祖先节点，新节点的起点在整个序列里的位置要加上祖先的长度。
如何理解问题3： few-shot 评测，不同任务各有一长串示例？

message.content: 如何理解问题3： few-shot 评测，不同任务各有一长串示例？

content.text:
**Few-shot** 是指在 prompt 里先放几个"问题 + 答案"的示例，再放真正要问的问题，让模型照着示例的格式和思路回答。**评测**是指用一批题目批量测试模型。

## 这种负载长什么样

以一个包含多个科目的评测集为例，每个科目有自己固定的一组示例：

```
物理科目的每个请求：
  [物理示例 1][物理示例 2]...[物理示例 5]  ← 约 2000 token，该科目所有题目都相同
  [待答的物理题]                            ← 约 100 token，每题不同

历史科目的每个请求：
  [历史示例 1][历史示例 2]...[历史示例 5]  ← 另一组 2000 token
  [待答的历史题]
```

所以请求天然分成若干组：
- **组内**：前 2000 个 token 完全相同，只有最后 100 个不同，共享比例约 95%。
- **组间**：从第一个 token 起就不同，完全无法共享。

在 radix tree 里就是：根下面每个科目一个长节点，每个长节点下面挂着很多短的叶子。

## 为什么调度顺序在这里影响很大

假设有 50 个科目，每科 100 道题，所有请求打乱后一起提交，而缓存只装得下几个科目的示例前缀。

- **FCFS**：相邻请求多半来自不同科目。物理的前缀刚缓存好，就被后面的历史、化学挤掉；下一道物理题到来时又要重算 2000 个 token。每个请求几乎都要完整 prefill 2100 个 token。
- **最长前缀匹配优先**：缓存里有物理的前缀时，等待队列里的物理题命中最长，全部优先放行。这 100 道题里只有第一道完整 prefill，其余 99 道各自只算约 100 个 token。物理做完再换下一个科目。

粗略算下来，prefill 的总量从"每题 2100 token"降到"每题略多于 100 token"，相差约 20 倍。

这就是我说它"收益最大"的原因：组内共享比例极高，组数又多到缓存装不下，同时评测是离线批量提交，不在乎单个请求的先后，调整顺序没有公平性的代价。
问题Q4： 投机解码中，大模型一次前向验证 k 个 token，耗时和生成 1 个差不多。这里是说小模型多次计算生成不同种k个token的序列，大模型能判断哪个是最好的？如果理解不对，应该如何理解？

message.content: 问题Q4： 投机解码中，大模型一次前向验证 k 个 token，耗时和生成 1 个差不多。这里是说小模型多次计算生成不同种k个token的序列，大模型能判断哪个是最好的？如果理解不对，应该如何理解？

lastPrompt: 问题Q4： 投机解码中，大模型一次前向验证 k 个 token，耗时和生成 1 个差不多。这里是说小模型多次计算生成不同种k个token的序列，大模型能判断哪个是最好的？如果理解不对，应该如何理解？

content.text:
理解不对。小模型不是生成多个候选序列让大模型挑，而是**只生成一条序列**，大模型逐位置检查"这个 token 是不是我自己也会生成的"。

## 一轮的过程

假设当前上下文是"今天天气"，k = 4。

**第 1 步：小模型起草。** 小模型自回归地跑 4 步，生成一条序列：

```
很  好  ，  适合
```

**第 2 步：大模型一次前向验证。** 把"今天天气 + 很 好 ， 适合"整个喂给大模型，做一次前向。因果注意力下，这一次前向会同时给出每个位置的"下一个 token"：

| 大模型看到的输入 | 大模型自己会输出 | 小模型猜的 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 今天天气 | 很 | 很 | 一致，接受 |
| 今天天气很 | 好 | 好 | 一致，接受 |
| 今天天气很好 | ， | ， | 一致，接受 |
| 今天天气很好， | 我们 | 适合 | 不一致，拒绝 |

**第 3 步：取最长的正确前缀。** 接受"很 好 ，"，丢弃"适合"，并直接采用大模型在这个位置的输出"我们"。

这一轮大模型只做了一次前向，却确认了 4 个 token（3 个接受的加 1 个自己纠正的）。下一轮从"今天天气很好，我们"继续。

## 三个要点

**为什么一次前向能验证 k 个位置**：这和 prefill 是同一件事。prefill 一次并行处理 N 个 token，每个位置都有输出，只是平时只用最后一个位置的输出。验证时把每个位置的输出都拿来用。

**为什么第一个不一致之后的全部丢弃**：后面位置的输出是在"前面的猜测都正确"的条件下算的。前面错了一个，后面的条件就不成立，结果作废。

**为什么耗时和生成 1 个差不多**：一次前向只读一遍权重，在带宽受限区间里，输入是 1 个 token 还是 5 个 token，耗时相差很小。

## 结果有保证

- 最坏情况：第一个就猜错，这一轮只得到大模型自己的 1 个 token，和不用投机解码一样，只是白花了小模型的时间。
- 最好情况：k 个全对，一轮得到 k + 1 个 token。
- 输出和大模型单独生成的完全一致，因为每个被接受的 token 都是大模型确认过的。

上面是贪心解码的情形。采样时不是比较"是否相同"，而是按两个模型给这个 token 的概率之比决定是否接受，可以证明输出分布仍与大模型一致。

你设想的"多个候选让大模型挑"也确实存在，是一类变体：起草时在每个位置给出多个候选，组成一棵树，大模型一次前向验证整棵树，取最长的被接受路径。它是在上述基本机制上提高接受率的改进，基本思想仍然是"验证"而不是"挑最好的"。
之所以让大模型一次前向验证 k个，是为了减少大模型一个个token生成的话，每次更新的KV Cache加载时间(前提是带宽受限)？

message.content: 之所以让大模型一次前向验证 k个，是为了减少大模型一个个token生成的话，每次更新的KV Cache加载时间(前提是带宽受限)？

content.text:
方向对了，但省下的主要不是 KV Cache 的读取，而是**模型权重的读取**。

## 每步 decode 读了什么

每做一次前向，GPU 要从显存读两样东西：

- **全部模型权重**：每一层的矩阵都要参与计算，一个不落。
- **这个请求的 KV Cache**：做注意力时读取。

用之前的例子比较大小：Qwen2.5-1.5B 的权重约 3 GB，一个 1000 token 上下文的 KV 约 28.7 MB。权重大了约 100 倍，所以单步耗时主要由读权重决定。

## 投机解码省的是什么

- **逐个生成 k 个 token**：k 次前向，权重读 k 遍。
- **一次验证 k 个 token**：1 次前向，权重读 1 遍。

省掉的是 k − 1 遍权重读取。KV 的读取也同样从 k 遍减到 1 遍，只是它占比小，是次要收益；上下文很长时 KV 的份量会上升，这部分收益也跟着变大。

所以你的那句话改成这样就准确了：

> 让大模型一次前向验证 k 个 token，是为了避免逐个生成时每一步都要把全部权重（以及 KV Cache）读一遍，前提是处在带宽受限区间。

## 一个用词上的区分

这里的"读"不是从硬盘加载到显存，权重和 KV 一直都在显存里。指的是每次前向时，数据从显存送到 GPU 计算单元的过程，它的速度上限就是显存带宽。之前算的"3070 上单请求最多约 150 步/秒"就是这个上限。

这也和 batching 是同一个道理：batching 让多个请求分摊一遍权重读取，投机解码让同一个请求的多个 token 分摊一遍权重读取。
这个权重矩阵群，为何要多次读取？对同一个大模型是不变的啊？

message.content: 这个权重矩阵群，为何要多次读取？对同一个大模型是不变的啊？

content.text:
权重确实不变，但"不变"只是说不用重新写入显存。**每次计算仍然要把它们取出来用一遍**，因为每一步的输入不同，计算必须重做。

## 计算本身要求数据经过计算单元

每一层的核心运算是矩阵乘向量：y = W·x。

- W 是权重，不变。
- x 是当前 token 的中间表示，每一步都不同。

要算出新的 y，W 的每一个元素都必须和新的 x 相乘。这意味着 W 的每个元素都要从显存被送到 GPU 的计算核心里参与一次乘法。物理上类比：同一个算符作用在不同的态上，算符没变，但每次作用都要用到它的全部矩阵元。

## 为什么不能"读一次就留在计算单元旁边"

GPU 内部的存储分两层：

- **显存**：容量大（你的 3070 是 8 GB），权重放在这里，但离计算核心"远"，读取速度受带宽限制。
- **芯片上的高速缓存**：紧挨计算核心，速度快，但只有几 MB 到几十 MB。

权重有 3 GB，缓存只装得下其中极小一部分。算第 1 层时读进来的权重，到算第 2 层时已经被挤出去了。所以每做一次前向，全部权重都要重新从显存流过一遍。

打个比方：权重是书架上的一套百科全书，缓存是只放得下几页纸的桌面。每回答一个新问题都要把整套书翻一遍，书的内容没变，但桌面留不住它。

## 能省的已经省了

- **算过的结果可以缓存**：过去 token 的中间结果就是 KV Cache，它们不用重算。
- **新 token 的计算是全新的**，没有可复用的结果，只能做一遍。

## 这也解释了为什么"分摊"有效

某一块权重被读到计算核心旁边时，可以趁它还在，连续和多个不同的 x 相乘：

- batching：和 8 个请求各自的 x 相乘；
- 投机解码的验证：和同一请求的 k 个 token 各自的 x 相乘。

读取只发生一次，乘法做了多次。读取是慢的那一环，乘法是快的那一环，所以多做几次乘法几乎不增加耗时。
GPU芯片上的高速缓存应该比HBM 显存还贵得多，是谁设计生产的？

message.content: GPU芯片上的高速缓存应该比HBM 显存还贵得多，是谁设计生产的？

lastPrompt: GPU芯片上的高速缓存应该比HBM 显存还贵得多，是谁设计生产的？

content.text:
是的，按每比特成本算，片上缓存比显存贵得多。它不是单独采购的器件，而是 **GPU 芯片本身的一部分**。

## 谁设计、谁生产

- **设计**：GPU 设计公司自己，比如 NVIDIA、AMD。缓存的容量、层级和布局是芯片架构的一部分。底层的存储单元通常基于晶圆代工厂或 IP 厂商（如 Synopsys、Arm）提供的标准设计。
- **生产**：晶圆代工厂，主要是台积电，部分产品由三星代工。缓存和计算核心在同一块硅片上，用同一套先进逻辑工艺一起制造。

## 和显存的区别

| | 片上缓存 | 显存 |
|---|---|---|
| 存储类型 | SRAM | DRAM |
| 每比特结构 | 6 个晶体管 | 1 个晶体管 + 1 个电容 |
| 位置 | 在 GPU 芯片内部 | 独立的芯片 |
| 生产者 | 台积电等代工厂（随 GPU 一起） | SK 海力士、三星、美光 |
| 容量 | 几 MB 到几十 MB | 几 GB 到上百 GB |

显存还分两种：
- **GDDR**：独立的内存颗粒，焊在显卡电路板上、GPU 芯片周围。你的 3070 用的是 GDDR6，不是 HBM。
- **HBM**：多层 DRAM 芯片垂直堆叠，和 GPU 芯片封装在一起，带宽高得多。用在数据中心级的 GPU 上。

## 为什么贵，又为什么不做大

- **贵**：SRAM 每比特用 6 个晶体管，占的面积远大于 DRAM，而且用的是最昂贵的先进逻辑工艺。
- **不做大**：一是面积会挤占计算核心的空间；二是缓存越大，访问越慢，就失去了"紧挨计算核心、速度快"的意义。

所以不可能靠加大片上缓存来装下几 GB 的权重，每次前向都要从显存读一遍权重是这个硬件结构决定的。提高 decode 速度的路只有两条：提高显存带宽（HBM 的意义所在），或者减少要读的字节数（量化的意义所在）。

## 层数

一个 decoder-only 模型是**一个** decoder，由 N 个结构相同的层堆叠而成。层数随模型规模增长：

| 模型 | 层数 |
|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | 24 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B / 7B | 28 |
| Llama 3 8B、Mistral 7B | 32 |
| DeepSeek-V3 | 61 |
| Llama 3 70B、Qwen2.5-72B | 80 |
| Llama 3.1 405B | 126 |

所以小模型二三十层，主流大模型 60–80 层，超大模型过百。

## 概率向量在哪一步产生

不是某次注意力算完后"决定"开始生成。注意力在每一层里都有，概率向量只在**走完全部 N 层之后**才产生，这是固定的结构：

```
token id
  ↓ 查嵌入表
隐藏向量（比如 1536 维）
  ↓
┌─ 第 1 层 ────────────────────────┐
│ 归一化 → 注意力（GQA）→ 加回残差 │
│ 归一化 → 前馈网络     → 加回残差 │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
  ↓
 ...（重复 N 层，每层权重各不相同）
  ↓
最后一层输出的隐藏向量
  ↓ 最终归一化
  ↓ 输出矩阵：隐藏维度 → 词表大小
logits（词表大小，比如 15 万维）
  ↓ 温度、top-p 等处理 + softmax
概率向量
  ↓ 采样
新 token
```

几点说明：

- **GQA 的位置**：它是每一层里注意力的一种实现方式，指多个查询头共用一组 K、V 头，比如 12 个查询头共用 2 个 KV 头。作用是缩小 KV Cache，对流程没有影响。
- **每层的注意力输出不是概率**，只是对隐藏向量的一次更新，加回残差后交给下一层继续加工。
- **只取最后一个位置**：最后一层在每个输入位置都有一个隐藏向量，生成时只把最后一个位置的向量送进输出矩阵。投机解码的验证则是把每个位置的都拿来用。

## 和前面内容的对应

- **KV 估算公式里的"层数"**：每一层的注意力各自缓存一份 K 和 V，所以要乘以层数；"KV 头数"就是 GQA 里共用的那组头的数量。
- **每步读一遍权重**：指的就是这 N 层的全部矩阵，再加上最后的输出矩阵。
- **结构化输出的掩码**：作用在 logits 这一步，softmax 之前。

message.content: 序列长N，attention矩阵是N*N维，什么时候开始生成 第N+1 新的token prob vector？

content.text:
**第 N 个位置的输出，就是第 N+1 个 token 的概率向量。** 不需要等 N×N 矩阵扩展到 N+1 行，它在处理这 N 个 token 的同一次前向里就产生了。

## 位置 i 的输出预测的是第 i+1 个 token

N×N 的注意力矩阵里，第 i 行表示"位置 i 对各位置的关注权重"。因果掩码让它只能看到自己和前面的位置，所以矩阵是下三角：

```
         被关注的位置
          1  2  3  4
位置 1  [ ■  ·  ·  · ]  → 输出预测第 2 个 token
位置 2  [ ■  ■  ·  · ]  → 输出预测第 3 个 token
位置 3  [ ■  ■  ■  · ]  → 输出预测第 4 个 token
位置 4  [ ■  ■  ■  ■ ]  → 输出预测第 5 个 token  ← 要的就是这个
```

每一行经过全部层之后，各自得到一个隐藏向量，含义是"读完前 i 个 token 后，对下一个 token 的预测"。模型训练时就是这样被要求的。

所以 N = 4 时：
- 前 3 行的输出预测的是第 2、3、4 个 token，这些是 prompt 里已知的，丢弃不用。
- 第 4 行的输出送进输出矩阵，得到第 5 个 token 的概率向量。

这就是 prefill：一次前向，每层算一个 N×N 的下三角注意力，最后只取最后一行的结果。

## 生成之后：每步只新增一行

采样出第 N+1 个 token 后，把它作为新输入。这时**不会重算**整个 (N+1)×(N+1) 矩阵，只算新增的那一行：

```
          1  2  3  4  5
位置 5  [ ■  ■  ■  ■  ■ ]  → 输出预测第 6 个 token
```

- 新 token 的查询向量，和前面所有位置的 K 做点积，得到这一行的权重，再对 V 加权求和。
- 前面位置的 K、V 直接从 KV Cache 里取。
- 前 4 行不用重算：因果掩码下它们看不到新 token，结果不会变。

这正是 KV Cache 成立的原因，也对应之前的结论：

| | 每层的注意力计算 | 计算量 |
|---|---|---|
| Prefill | N 行，完整的下三角 | 随 N 平方增长 |
| Decode 每步 | 只算 1 行 | 随 N 线性增长 |

投机解码的验证、chunked prefill 也都是这张图：一次算新增的 k 行，每一行的输出都是对下一个 token 的预测。

369	    def match_prefix(self, params: MatchPrefixParams) -> MatchResult:
370	        """Find the longest cached prefix of ``key`` in the radix tree.
371	
372	        The logical namespace for prefix matching is determined by both the
373	        token id sequence and the optional ``extra_key`` carried by ``RadixKey``.
374	        Entries that share identical leading token ids but have *different*
375	        ``extra_key`` values are intentionally kept disjoint and never share
376	        prefix nodes. This is useful to:
377	
378	        * Isolate KV cache lines for different LoRA / adapter IDs.
379	        * Separate requests that intentionally should not share state (e.g.,
380	          different sampling salt, cache version, or retrieval augmentation
381	          context) by supplying a distinct ``extra_key``.
382	
383	        Args:
384	            params (MatchPrefixParams): Parameters containing the lookup key
385	                with a list of token ids and an optional ``extra_key`` namespace tag.
386	                If ``page_size > 1`` the length is internally truncated to a multiple
387	                of ``page_size`` before matching. Passing an empty key returns an
388	                empty result with the root as the last node.
389	
390	        Returns:
391	            MatchResult: ``device_prefix_len`` is the length of the longest
392	            cached prefix (may be 0).
393	            ``last_device_node`` and ``last_host_node`` (currently the same) are the tree node objects
394	            representing the terminal node of the matched prefix. This method
395	            may mutate internal structure by splitting an existing node if the
396	            match ends inside a stored segment.
397	
398	        Internal updates:
399	            * Refreshes access metadata (timestamps) used by the
400	                configured eviction strategy.
401	            * If the lookup ends inside a stored segment the node is split once
402	                to expose a precise boundary; this structural refinement improves
403	                subsequent match efficiency and does not duplicate data.
404	        """
405	        key = params.key
406	        key, _ = key.maybe_to_bigram_view(self.is_eagle)
407	
408	        if self.disable or len(key) == 0:
409	            return self._empty_match_result
410	
411	        key = key.page_aligned(self.page_size)
412	
413	        if len(key) == 0:
414	            return self._empty_match_result
415	
416	        value, last_node = self._match_prefix_helper(self.root_node, key)
417	        return MatchResult(
418	            device_prefix_len=sum(len(v) for v in value),
419	            last_device_node=last_node,
420	            last_host_node=last_node,
421	            best_match_node=last_node,
422	        )
423	
424	    def touch_prefix(self, key: RadixKey) -> None:
425	        key, _ = key.maybe_to_bigram_view(self.is_eagle)
426	        if self.disable or len(key) == 0:
427	            return
428	        key = key.page_aligned(self.page_size)
429	        if len(key) == 0:
430	            return
431	        self._match_prefix_helper(self.root_node, key)

433	    def insert(self, params: InsertParams) -> InsertResult:
434	        if self.disable:
435	            return InsertResult(prefix_len=0)
436	
437	        key = params.key
438	        value = params.value
439	        priority = params.priority
440	        inserted_len = params.inserted_len
441	
442	        key, value = key.maybe_to_bigram_view(self.is_eagle, value)
443	        key = key.page_aligned(self.page_size)
444	        if value is not None:
445	            value = value[: len(key)]
446	        else:
447	            # Debug/test fallback: use token ids themselves as values.
448	            value = torch.tensor(key.token_ids[: len(key)], dtype=torch.int64)
449	
450	        prefix_len, last_node = self._insert_helper(
451	            self.root_node, key, value, priority, inserted_len
452	        )
453	        return InsertResult(prefix_len=prefix_len, last_device_node=last_node)

455	    def _insert_cache(
456	        self,
457	        req: Req,
458	        token_ids,
459	        *,
460	        key_limit: Optional[int] = None,
461	        split_prompt: bool = False,
462	    ) -> Tuple[RadixKey, torch.Tensor, int]:
463	        """Insert the page-aligned key of ``token_ids`` (cut at ``key_limit``)
464	        and free the duplicates it exposed; returns (key, row slice, matched)."""
465	        kv_indices = self.req_to_token_pool.req_to_token[
466	            req.kv.req_pool_idx, : len(token_ids)
467	        ]
468	        radix_key = RadixKey(
469	            token_ids,
470	            req.extra_key,
471	            is_bigram=self.is_eagle,
472	            cache_salt=req.cache_salt,
473	        ).page_aligned(self.page_size)
474	        if key_limit is not None:
475	            radix_key = radix_key[:key_limit]
476	        key_len = len(radix_key)
477	        values = kv_indices[:key_len].to(dtype=torch.int64, copy=True)
478	
479	        # Radix Cache takes one ref in memory pool
480	        priority = req.priority or 0
481	        result = self.insert(
482	            InsertParams(
483	                key=radix_key,
484	                value=values,
485	                inserted_len=req.kv.cache_inserted_len,
486	                priority=priority,
487	            )
488	        )
489	        req.kv.record_insert(key_len)
490	        if split_prompt:
491	            # Split the leaf at the prompt boundary so eviction can drop the
492	            # output KV without the prompt; a prefix re-insert only changes topology.
493	            prompt_key = RadixKey(
494	                token_ids[: len(req.origin_input_ids)],
495	                req.extra_key,
496	                is_bigram=self.is_eagle,
497	                cache_salt=req.cache_salt,
498	            ).page_aligned(self.page_size)
499	            if 0 < len(prompt_key) < key_len:
500	                self.insert(
501	                    InsertParams(
502	                        key=prompt_key,
503	                        value=values[: len(prompt_key)],
504	                        inserted_len=len(prompt_key),
505	                        priority=min(priority + 1, torch.iinfo(torch.int64).max),
506	                    )
507	                )
508	
509	        self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free_segment(
510	            kv_indices[req.kv.cache_protected_len : result.prefix_len],
511	            start_pos=req.kv.cache_protected_len,
512	        )
513	        return radix_key, kv_indices, result.prefix_len
514	
515	    def checkpoint(self, req: Req, *, up_to: int):
516	        if self.disable:
517	            return
518	        token_ids = req.full_untruncated_fill_ids[:up_to]
519	        # Pure-SWA trees never cache what the window already evicted.
520	        window_evict_floor = req.kv.window_evict_floor
521	        key_limit = (
522	            ceil_align(window_evict_floor, self.page_size)
523	            if window_evict_floor > 0
524	            else None
525	        )
526	        radix_key, _, _ = self._insert_cache(
527	            req, token_ids, key_limit=key_limit, split_prompt=True
528	        )
529	
530	        # The prefix indices could be updated, reuse it
531	        match_result = self.match_prefix(MatchPrefixParams(key=radix_key))
532	        new_last_node = match_result.last_device_node
533	        new_indices = self.path_device_indices(new_last_node)
534	        assert len(new_indices) == len(radix_key), (
535	            f"{len(new_indices)=}, {len(radix_key)=}"
536	        )
537	
538	        self.req_to_token_pool.write(
539	            (req.kv.req_pool_idx, slice(req.kv.cache_protected_len, len(new_indices))),
540	            new_indices[req.kv.cache_protected_len :],
541	        )
542	
543	        # With page_size > 1 the partial page stays in the request's row but not
544	        # in the tree; cache_protected_len marks the tree-owned part so the next
545	        # checkpoint or release_kv_cache frees the rest.
546	        req.kv.protect_prefix(len(new_indices))
547	
548	        self.unlock(req.lock)
549	        req.lock = self.lock(new_last_node)
550	        req.last_node = new_last_node

559	    def evict(self, params: EvictParams) -> EvictResult:
560	        if self.disable:
561	            return EvictResult()
562	
563	        start_time = time.perf_counter()
564	        num_tokens = params.num_tokens
565	        leaves = list(self.evictable_leaves)
566	        eviction_heap = [
567	            (self.eviction_strategy.get_priority(node), node) for node in leaves
568	        ]
569	        heapq.heapify(eviction_heap)
570	
571	        num_evicted = 0
572	        while num_evicted < num_tokens and len(eviction_heap):
573	            _priority, x = heapq.heappop(eviction_heap)
574	
575	            # Tree values are page-aligned copies of a kv row: page-exact segment.
576	            self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free_segment(x.value, start_pos=0)
577	            num_evicted += len(x.value)
578	            self._delete_leaf(x)
579	
580	            if len(x.parent.children) == 0 and x.parent.lock_ref == 0:
581	                new_priority = self.eviction_strategy.get_priority(x.parent)
582	                heapq.heappush(eviction_heap, (new_priority, x.parent))
583	
584	            self.kv_events.record_remove(x)
585	
586	        self.update_eviction_metrics(num_evicted, start_time)
587	        return EvictResult(num_tokens_evicted=num_evicted)
588	
589	    def inc_lock_ref(self, node: TreeNode) -> IncLockRefResult:
590	        if self.disable:
591	            return IncLockRefResult(delta=0)
592	
593	        delta = 0
594	        while node != self.root_node:
595	            if node.lock_ref == 0:
596	                self.evictable_size_ -= len(node.key)
597	                self.protected_size_ += len(node.key)
598	                delta -= len(node.key)
599	            node.lock_ref += 1
600	            self._update_leaf_status(node)
601	            node = node.parent
602	        return IncLockRefResult(delta=delta)
603	
604	    def dec_lock_ref(
605	        self, node: TreeNode, params: Optional[DecLockRefParams] = None
606	    ) -> DecLockRefResult:
607	        if self.disable:
608	            return DecLockRefResult(delta=0)
609	
610	        delta = 0
611	        while node != self.root_node:
612	            if node.lock_ref == 1:
613	                self.evictable_size_ += len(node.key)
614	                self.protected_size_ -= len(node.key)
615	                delta += len(node.key)
616	            node.lock_ref -= 1
617	            self._update_leaf_status(node)
618	            if node.parent is None:
619	                assert node is self.root_node, (
620	                    "This request holds the node from another tree"
621	                )
622	            node = node.parent
623	        return DecLockRefResult(delta=delta)

648	    def path_device_indices(self, node: TreeNode) -> torch.Tensor:
649	        values = []
650	        while node is not self.root_node:
651	            values.append(node.value)
652	            node = node.parent
653	        if not values:
654	            return self._empty_device_indices
655	        values.reverse()

658	    def _match_prefix_helper(self, node: TreeNode, key: RadixKey):
659	        access_time = time.monotonic()
660	        node.last_access_time = access_time
661	
662	        child_key = key.child_key(self.page_size)
663	
664	        value = []
665	        while len(key) > 0 and child_key in node.children.keys():
666	            child = node.children[child_key]
667	            child.last_access_time = access_time
668	            prefix_len = child.key.match(key, page_size=self.page_size)
669	            if prefix_len < len(child.key):
670	                new_node = self._split_node(child.key, child, prefix_len)
671	                value.append(new_node.value)
672	                node = new_node
673	                break
674	            else:
675	                value.append(child.value)
676	                node = child
677	                key = key[prefix_len:]
678	
679	                if len(key):
680	                    child_key = key.child_key(self.page_size)
681	
682	        return value, node
683	
684	    def _split_node(self, key: RadixKey, child: TreeNode, split_len: int):
685	        # new_node -> child
686	        # New node inherits child's priority (represents shared prefix)
687	        new_node = TreeNode(priority=child.priority)
688	        new_node.hit_count = child.hit_count
689	        new_node.children = {key[split_len:].child_key(self.page_size): child}
690	        new_node.parent = child.parent
691	        new_node.lock_ref = child.lock_ref
692	        new_node.key = child.key[:split_len]
693	        new_node.value = child.value[:split_len].clone()
694	        child.parent = new_node
695	        child.key = child.key[split_len:]
696	        child.value = child.value[split_len:].clone()
697	        new_node.parent.children[key.child_key(self.page_size)] = new_node
698	
699	        # Split hash_value if it was already computed, otherwise leave as None
700	        new_node.hash_value, child.hash_value = split_node_hash_value(
701	            child.hash_value, split_len, self.page_size
702	        )
703	        new_node.event_hash_value, child.event_hash_value = split_node_hash_value(
704	            child.event_hash_value, split_len, self.page_size
705	        )
706	
707	        return new_node
708	
709	    def _inc_hit_count(self, node: TreeNode):
710	        node.hit_count += 1
711	
712	    def _insert_helper(
713	        self,
714	        node: TreeNode,
715	        key: RadixKey,
716	        value,
717	        priority: int = 0,
718	        inserted_len: int = 0,
719	    ):
720	        # Convert None priority to 0
721	        if priority is None:
722	            priority = 0
723	        access_time = time.monotonic()
724	        node.last_access_time = access_time
725	        # Update priority along the path (take max to propagate higher priority)
726	        node.priority = max(node.priority, priority)
727	        if len(key) == 0:
728	            return 0, node
729	
730	        child_key = key.child_key(self.page_size)
731	
732	        total_prefix_length = 0
733	        while len(key) > 0 and child_key in node.children.keys():
734	            node = node.children[child_key]
735	            node.last_access_time = access_time
736	            prefix_len = node.key.match(key, page_size=self.page_size)
737	            total_prefix_length += prefix_len
738	            key = key[prefix_len:]
739	            value = value[prefix_len:]
740	
741	            if prefix_len < len(node.key):
742	                new_node = self._split_node(node.key, node, prefix_len)
743	                new_node.priority = max(new_node.priority, priority)
744	                node = new_node
745	            else:
746	                node.priority = max(node.priority, priority)
747	            # Nodes this request already inserted were counted back then.
748	            if total_prefix_length > inserted_len:
749	                self._inc_hit_count(node)
750	            if len(key):
751	                child_key = key.child_key(self.page_size)
752	
753	        if len(key):
754	            new_node = TreeNode(priority=priority)
755	            new_node.parent = node
756	            new_node.key = key
757	            new_node.value = value.clone()
758	            if total_prefix_length + len(key) > inserted_len:
759	                self._inc_hit_count(new_node)
760	            node.children[child_key] = new_node
761	            self.evictable_size_ += len(key)
762	            self._update_leaf_status(node)
763	            self._update_leaf_status(new_node)
764	            # Hash will be computed lazily during event emission
765	            self.kv_events.record_store(new_node)
766	            node = new_node
767	        return total_prefix_length, node
768	
769	    def _print_helper(self, node: TreeNode, indent: int):
770	        """Prints the radix tree in a human-readable format."""
771	        stack = [(node, indent)]
772	        while stack:
773	            current_node, current_indent = stack.pop()
774	            print(
775	                " " * current_indent,
776	                len(current_node.key),
777	                current_node.key.token_ids[:10],
778	                f"r={current_node.lock_ref}",
779	            )
780	            for key, child in current_node.children.items():
781	                stack.append((child, current_indent + 2))
782	
783	                assert key == child.key.child_key(self.page_size), (
784	                    f"{key=}, {child.key.child_key(self.page_size)=}"
785	                )
786	
787	    def _delete_leaf(self, node):
788	        key = node.key.child_key(self.page_size)
789	        v = node.parent.children.pop(key, None)
790	        assert v == node, f"parent does not have child key, {key}"
791	
792	        self.evictable_size_ -= len(node.key)
793	        if node in self.evictable_leaves:
794	            self.evictable_leaves.remove(node)
795	        self._update_leaf_status(node.parent)
796	
797	    def _update_leaf_status(self, node: TreeNode):
798	        if node.evicted or node.lock_ref > 0:
799	            if node in self.evictable_leaves:
800	                self.evictable_leaves.remove(node)
801	            return
802	
803	        for child in node.children.values():
804	            if not child.evicted:
805	                if node in self.evictable_leaves:
806	                    self.evictable_leaves.remove(node)
807	                return
808	
809	        if node not in self.evictable_leaves:
810	            self.evictable_leaves.add(node)
811	
812	    def _total_size_helper(self):
813	        total_size = 0
814	        stack = [self.root_node]
815	        while stack:
816	            current_node = stack.pop()
817	            total_size += len(current_node.value)
818	            for child in current_node.children.values():
819	                if child.evicted:
820	                    continue
821	                stack.append(child)
822	        return total_size

"""
The radix tree data structure for managing the KV cache.
"""

import heapq
import logging
import sys
import time
from array import array
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Iterator, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

import torch

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

from sglang.srt.layers.cp.base import get_cp_strategy, is_cp_sharded_padded
from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import (
    BasePrefixCache,
    DecLockRefParams,
    DecLockRefResult,
    EvictParams,
    EvictResult,
    IncLockRefResult,
    InsertParams,
    InsertResult,
    MatchPrefixParams,
    MatchResult,
)
from sglang.srt.mem_cache.events import KVCacheEventRecorder, LoRANameTable
from sglang.srt.mem_cache.utils import (
    get_eviction_strategy,
    split_node_hash_value,
)
from sglang.srt.utils.common import ceil_align

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import Req


class RadixKey:
    """is_bigram=True: token_ids holds raw tokens (N+1 for N bigrams); slices share one boundary token."""

    __slots__ = ("token_ids", "extra_key", "cache_salt", "is_bigram", "limit")

    def __init__(
        self,
        token_ids: array[int],
        extra_key: Optional[str] = None,
        is_bigram: bool = False,
        limit: Optional[int] = None,
        cache_salt: Optional[str] = None,
    ):
        # token ids sequence (raw ints in both modes)
        self.token_ids = token_ids
        # Namespaces the tree and storage; KV events see only its LoRA name.
        self.extra_key = extra_key
        # Namespaces the tree, storage and KV events.
        self.cache_salt = cache_salt or None
        # bigram view over token_ids: length = max(0, len(token_ids) - 1)
        self.is_bigram = is_bigram
        # Optional cap on raw tokens: behave as if token_ids were sliced to
        # token_ids[:limit], without the O(n) copy. None = use all tokens.
        self.limit = limit

    def _raw_len(self) -> int:
        n = len(self.token_ids)
        if self.limit is not None and self.limit < n:
            return self.limit
        return n

    def raw_token_ids(self) -> array:
        """token_ids honoring `limit` (copies only when capped)."""
        n = self._raw_len()
        t = self.token_ids
        return t if n == len(t) else t[:n]

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        n = self._raw_len()
        if self.is_bigram:
            return n - 1 if n > 0 else 0
        return n

    # TODO(Jialin): vectorize with numpy without PyLong boxing
    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator:
        t = self.token_ids
        n = self._raw_len()
        if self.is_bigram:
            for i in range(n - 1 if n > 0 else 0):
                yield (t[i], t[i + 1])
        elif n == len(t):
            yield from t
        else:
            for i in range(n):
                yield t[i]

    def __getitem__(self, idx: Union[int, slice]) -> RadixKey:
        # Normalize int -> 1-element slice so the rest handles one shape.
        if isinstance(idx, int):
            if idx < 0:
                idx += len(self)
            if idx < 0 or idx >= len(self):
                raise IndexError(f"RadixKey index out of range: {idx}")
            idx = slice(idx, idx + 1)
        start, stop, step = idx.indices(len(self))
        if step != 1:
            raise ValueError("RadixKey slice step must be 1")

        if self.is_bigram:
            # bigrams [start, stop) span raw tokens [start, stop + 1);
            # empty slice -> empty raw tokens (not a dangling boundary token).
            raw = self.token_ids[start : stop + 1] if stop > start else array("q")
            return RadixKey(
                raw,
                self.extra_key,
                is_bigram=True,
                cache_salt=self.cache_salt,
            )
        return RadixKey(
            self.token_ids[start:stop],
            self.extra_key,
            cache_salt=self.cache_salt,
        )

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        preview = self.token_ids[:10]
        return f"RadixKey(extra_key={self.extra_key!r}, cache_salt={self.cache_salt!r}, token_ids={preview}{'...' if len(self.token_ids) > 10 else ''}, is_bigram={self.is_bigram})"

    def page_aligned(self, page_size: int) -> RadixKey:
        if page_size == 1:
            return self
        aligned_len = len(self) // page_size * page_size
        return self[:aligned_len]

    def maybe_to_bigram_view(
        self,
        is_eagle: bool,
        value: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
    ) -> Tuple[RadixKey, Optional[torch.Tensor]]:
        # O(1): flip the bigram flag instead of materializing a tuple list.
        # value is paired with raw tokens and gets truncated to the bigram count.
        if is_eagle and not self.is_bigram:
            self.is_bigram = True
            if value is not None:
                value = value[: len(self)]
        return self, value

    def _check_compatible(self, other: RadixKey) -> None:
        if self.extra_key != other.extra_key:
            raise ValueError(
                f"RadixKey operations require matching extra_key, but got "
                f"{self.extra_key=} != {other.extra_key=}"
            )
        if self.cache_salt != other.cache_salt:
            raise ValueError(
                f"RadixKey operations require matching cache_salt, but got "
                f"{self.cache_salt=} != {other.cache_salt=}"
            )

    def match(self, other: RadixKey, page_size: int = 1) -> int:
        """Logical-unit prefix length shared with ``other``. Result is rounded down to ``page_size``."""
        return self.match_at(other, offset=0, page_size=page_size)

    def match_at(self, other: RadixKey, offset: int, page_size: int = 1) -> int:
        """Match without slicing while preserving bigram boundaries and limit semantics."""
        self._check_compatible(other)
        if self.is_bigram != other.is_bigram:
            raise ValueError("RadixKey operations require matching bigram modes")
        if offset < 0 or offset > len(other):
            raise IndexError(f"RadixKey offset out of range: {offset}")
        t0, t1 = self.token_ids, other.token_ids
        assert type(t0) is type(t1), (type(t0), type(t1))
        n = min(self._raw_len(), other._raw_len() - offset)

        # Exponential search for the first diverging token: gallop in doubling
        # windows (one C-level slice compare each), then binary-search the window
        # holding the divergence -- no per-token Python loop on long shared prefixes.
        matched_tokens = n
        lo = 0
        step = 1
        while lo < n:
            hi = lo + step if lo + step < n else n
            if t0[lo:hi] != t1[offset + lo : offset + hi]:
                while hi - lo > 1:
                    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
                    if t0[lo:mid] == t1[offset + lo : offset + mid]:
                        lo = mid
                    else:
                        hi = mid
                matched_tokens = lo
                break
            lo = hi
            step *= 2

        if self.is_bigram:
            matched = max(0, min(matched_tokens - 1, len(self), len(other) - offset))
            return (matched // page_size) * page_size if page_size > 1 else matched

        matched_tokens = min(matched_tokens, len(self), len(other) - offset)
        if page_size == 1:
            return matched_tokens
        return (matched_tokens // page_size) * page_size

    def child_key(self, page_size: int = 1):
        """Hashable dict-key for the first ``page_size`` logical units, namespaced by ``extra_key``."""
        return self.child_key_at(offset=0, page_size=page_size)

    def child_key_at(self, offset: int, page_size: int = 1):
        """Hashable child key at ``offset`` without slicing token storage."""
        if offset < 0 or offset + page_size > len(self):
            raise IndexError(
                f"RadixKey child range out of bounds: offset={offset}, "
                f"page_size={page_size}, len={len(self)}"
            )
        t = self.token_ids
        if self.is_bigram:
            if page_size == 1:
                plain = (t[offset], t[offset + 1])
            else:
                plain = tuple(
                    (t[j], t[j + 1]) for j in range(offset, offset + page_size)
                )
        else:
            plain = (
                t[offset] if page_size == 1 else tuple(t[offset : offset + page_size])
            )
        if self.cache_salt is not None:
            return ((self.extra_key, self.cache_salt), plain)
        return plain if self.extra_key is None else (self.extra_key, plain)


class TreeNode:
    counter = 0

    def __init__(self, id: Optional[int] = None, priority: int = 0):
        self.children = defaultdict(TreeNode)
        self.parent: TreeNode = None
        self.key: RadixKey = None
        self.value: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
        self.lock_ref = 0
        self.last_access_time = time.monotonic()
        self.creation_time = time.monotonic()

        self.hit_count = 0
        # store hash values of each pages
        self.hash_value: Optional[List[str]] = None
        # Namespace-aware hashes used only for external KV events.
        self.event_hash_value: Optional[List[str]] = None
        # priority for priority-aware eviction
        self.priority = priority

        self.id = TreeNode.counter if id is None else id
        TreeNode.counter += 1

    @property
    def evicted(self):
        return self.value is None

    def __lt__(self, other: TreeNode):
        return self.last_access_time < other.last_access_time


class RadixCache(BasePrefixCache):
    def __init__(self, params: CacheInitParams):
        self.disable = params.disable
        self.req_to_token_pool = params.req_to_token_pool
        self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator = params.token_to_kv_pool_allocator
        self.page_size = params.page_size
        self.is_eagle = params.is_eagle
        self.eviction_policy = params.eviction_policy.lower()

        # A disabled tree holds nothing, so it reports no KV events and never
        # evicts; its eviction policy config is not built or validated.
        self.kv_events = KVCacheEventRecorder(
            enabled=params.enable_kv_cache_events and not self.disable,
            page_size=self.page_size,
            dynamo_format=params.dynamo_kv_event_format,
            lora_names=params.kv_event_lora_names,
        )

        if params.enable_metrics:
            self.init_metrics_collector()

        if self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator:
            self.logical_page_size = self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.page_size
            dev = self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.device
            if isinstance(dev, (str, torch.device)):
                self.device = torch.device(dev)
            else:
                self.device = torch.device("cpu")
        else:
            self.logical_page_size = self.page_size
            self.device = torch.device("cpu")
        if is_cp_sharded_padded():
            self.logical_page_size *= get_cp_strategy().cp_size

        self.eviction_strategy = get_eviction_strategy(
            "lru" if self.disable else self.eviction_policy,
            None if self.disable else params.eviction_policy_config,
        )

        self.evictable_leaves = set()
        self.reset()

    @classmethod
    def create_simulated(
        self,
        disable: bool = False,
        mock_allocator: Optional[Any] = None,
        page_size: int = 1,
        enable_kv_cache_events: bool = False,
        dynamo_kv_event_format: bool = False,
        kv_event_lora_names: Optional[LoRANameTable] = None,
    ) -> RadixCache:
        """Init a radix cache without memory pools for simulation purpose."""
        params = CacheInitParams(
            disable=disable,
            req_to_token_pool=None,
            token_to_kv_pool_allocator=mock_allocator,
            page_size=page_size,
            enable_kv_cache_events=enable_kv_cache_events,
            dynamo_kv_event_format=dynamo_kv_event_format,
            kv_event_lora_names=kv_event_lora_names,
        )
        return RadixCache(params)

    ##### Public API #####

    def reset(self):
        # Initialize root with minimum priority so any real priority overrides it
        self.root_node = TreeNode(priority=-sys.maxsize)
        self.root_node.key = RadixKey(token_ids=array("q"), extra_key=None)
        self.root_node.value = []
        self.root_node.lock_ref = 1
        self.root_node.hash_value = []
        self.evictable_size_ = 0
        self.protected_size_ = 0
        self.evictable_leaves.clear()
        self._empty_device_indices = torch.empty(
            (0,), dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device
        )
        self._empty_match_result = MatchResult(
            device_prefix_len=0,
            last_device_node=self.root_node,
            last_host_node=self.root_node,
            best_match_node=self.root_node,
        )
        self.kv_events.record_all_cleared()

    def match_prefix(self, params: MatchPrefixParams) -> MatchResult:
        """Find the longest cached prefix of ``key`` in the radix tree.

        The logical namespace for prefix matching is determined by both the
        token id sequence and the optional ``extra_key`` carried by ``RadixKey``.
        Entries that share identical leading token ids but have *different*
        ``extra_key`` values are intentionally kept disjoint and never share
        prefix nodes. This is useful to:

        * Isolate KV cache lines for different LoRA / adapter IDs.
        * Separate requests that intentionally should not share state (e.g.,
          different sampling salt, cache version, or retrieval augmentation
          context) by supplying a distinct ``extra_key``.

        Args:
            params (MatchPrefixParams): Parameters containing the lookup key
                with a list of token ids and an optional ``extra_key`` namespace tag.
                If ``page_size > 1`` the length is internally truncated to a multiple
                of ``page_size`` before matching. Passing an empty key returns an
                empty result with the root as the last node.

        Returns:
            MatchResult: ``device_prefix_len`` is the length of the longest
            cached prefix (may be 0).
            ``last_device_node`` and ``last_host_node`` (currently the same) are the tree node objects
            representing the terminal node of the matched prefix. This method
            may mutate internal structure by splitting an existing node if the
            match ends inside a stored segment.

        Internal updates:
            * Refreshes access metadata (timestamps) used by the
                configured eviction strategy.
            * If the lookup ends inside a stored segment the node is split once
                to expose a precise boundary; this structural refinement improves
                subsequent match efficiency and does not duplicate data.
        """
        key = params.key
        key, _ = key.maybe_to_bigram_view(self.is_eagle)

        if self.disable or len(key) == 0:
            return self._empty_match_result

        key = key.page_aligned(self.page_size)

        if len(key) == 0:
            return self._empty_match_result

        value, last_node = self._match_prefix_helper(self.root_node, key)
        return MatchResult(
            device_prefix_len=sum(len(v) for v in value),
            last_device_node=last_node,
            last_host_node=last_node,
            best_match_node=last_node,
        )

    def touch_prefix(self, key: RadixKey) -> None:
        key, _ = key.maybe_to_bigram_view(self.is_eagle)
        if self.disable or len(key) == 0:
            return
        key = key.page_aligned(self.page_size)
        if len(key) == 0:
            return
        self._match_prefix_helper(self.root_node, key)

    def insert(self, params: InsertParams) -> InsertResult:
        if self.disable:
            return InsertResult(prefix_len=0)

        key = params.key
        value = params.value
        priority = params.priority
        inserted_len = params.inserted_len

        key, value = key.maybe_to_bigram_view(self.is_eagle, value)
        key = key.page_aligned(self.page_size)
        if value is not None:
            value = value[: len(key)]
        else:
            # Debug/test fallback: use token ids themselves as values.
            value = torch.tensor(key.token_ids[: len(key)], dtype=torch.int64)

        prefix_len, last_node = self._insert_helper(
            self.root_node, key, value, priority, inserted_len
        )
        return InsertResult(prefix_len=prefix_len, last_device_node=last_node)

    def _insert_cache(
        self,
        req: Req,
        token_ids,
        *,
        key_limit: Optional[int] = None,
        split_prompt: bool = False,
    ) -> Tuple[RadixKey, torch.Tensor, int]:
        """Insert the page-aligned key of ``token_ids`` (cut at ``key_limit``)
        and free the duplicates it exposed; returns (key, row slice, matched)."""
        kv_indices = self.req_to_token_pool.req_to_token[
            req.kv.req_pool_idx, : len(token_ids)
        ]
        radix_key = RadixKey(
            token_ids,
            req.extra_key,
            is_bigram=self.is_eagle,
            cache_salt=req.cache_salt,
        ).page_aligned(self.page_size)
        if key_limit is not None:
            radix_key = radix_key[:key_limit]
        key_len = len(radix_key)
        values = kv_indices[:key_len].to(dtype=torch.int64, copy=True)

        # Radix Cache takes one ref in memory pool
        priority = req.priority or 0
        result = self.insert(
            InsertParams(
                key=radix_key,
                value=values,
                inserted_len=req.kv.cache_inserted_len,
                priority=priority,
            )
        )
        req.kv.record_insert(key_len)
        if split_prompt:
            # Split the leaf at the prompt boundary so eviction can drop the
            # output KV without the prompt; a prefix re-insert only changes topology.
            prompt_key = RadixKey(
                token_ids[: len(req.origin_input_ids)],
                req.extra_key,
                is_bigram=self.is_eagle,
                cache_salt=req.cache_salt,
            ).page_aligned(self.page_size)
            if 0 < len(prompt_key) < key_len:
                self.insert(
                    InsertParams(
                        key=prompt_key,
                        value=values[: len(prompt_key)],
                        inserted_len=len(prompt_key),
                        priority=min(priority + 1, torch.iinfo(torch.int64).max),
                    )
                )

        self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free_segment(
            kv_indices[req.kv.cache_protected_len : result.prefix_len],
            start_pos=req.kv.cache_protected_len,
        )
        return radix_key, kv_indices, result.prefix_len

    def checkpoint(self, req: Req, *, up_to: int):
        if self.disable:
            return
        token_ids = req.full_untruncated_fill_ids[:up_to]
        # Pure-SWA trees never cache what the window already evicted.
        window_evict_floor = req.kv.window_evict_floor
        key_limit = (
            ceil_align(window_evict_floor, self.page_size)
            if window_evict_floor > 0
            else None
        )
        radix_key, _, _ = self._insert_cache(
            req, token_ids, key_limit=key_limit, split_prompt=True
        )

        # The prefix indices could be updated, reuse it
        match_result = self.match_prefix(MatchPrefixParams(key=radix_key))
        new_last_node = match_result.last_device_node
        new_indices = self.path_device_indices(new_last_node)
        assert len(new_indices) == len(radix_key), (
            f"{len(new_indices)=}, {len(radix_key)=}"
        )

        self.req_to_token_pool.write(
            (req.kv.req_pool_idx, slice(req.kv.cache_protected_len, len(new_indices))),
            new_indices[req.kv.cache_protected_len :],
        )

        # With page_size > 1 the partial page stays in the request's row but not
        # in the tree; cache_protected_len marks the tree-owned part so the next
        # checkpoint or release_kv_cache frees the rest.
        req.kv.protect_prefix(len(new_indices))

        self.unlock(req.lock)
        req.lock = self.lock(new_last_node)
        req.last_node = new_last_node

    def pretty_print(self):
        self._print_helper(self.root_node, 0)
        print(f"#tokens: {self.total_size()}")

    def total_size(self):
        return self._total_size_helper()

    def evict(self, params: EvictParams) -> EvictResult:
        if self.disable:
            return EvictResult()

        start_time = time.perf_counter()
        num_tokens = params.num_tokens
        leaves = list(self.evictable_leaves)
        eviction_heap = [
            (self.eviction_strategy.get_priority(node), node) for node in leaves
        ]
        heapq.heapify(eviction_heap)

        num_evicted = 0
        while num_evicted < num_tokens and len(eviction_heap):
            _priority, x = heapq.heappop(eviction_heap)

            # Tree values are page-aligned copies of a kv row: page-exact segment.
            self.token_to_kv_pool_allocator.free_segment(x.value, start_pos=0)
            num_evicted += len(x.value)
            self._delete_leaf(x)

            if len(x.parent.children) == 0 and x.parent.lock_ref == 0:
                new_priority = self.eviction_strategy.get_priority(x.parent)
                heapq.heappush(eviction_heap, (new_priority, x.parent))

            self.kv_events.record_remove(x)

        self.update_eviction_metrics(num_evicted, start_time)
        return EvictResult(num_tokens_evicted=num_evicted)

    def inc_lock_ref(self, node: TreeNode) -> IncLockRefResult:
        if self.disable:
            return IncLockRefResult(delta=0)

        delta = 0
        while node != self.root_node:
            if node.lock_ref == 0:
                self.evictable_size_ -= len(node.key)
                self.protected_size_ += len(node.key)
                delta -= len(node.key)
            node.lock_ref += 1
            self._update_leaf_status(node)
            node = node.parent
        return IncLockRefResult(delta=delta)

    def dec_lock_ref(
        self, node: TreeNode, params: Optional[DecLockRefParams] = None
    ) -> DecLockRefResult:
        if self.disable:
            return DecLockRefResult(delta=0)

        delta = 0
        while node != self.root_node:
            if node.lock_ref == 1:
                self.evictable_size_ += len(node.key)
                self.protected_size_ -= len(node.key)
                delta += len(node.key)
            node.lock_ref -= 1
            self._update_leaf_status(node)
            if node.parent is None:
                assert node is self.root_node, (
                    "This request holds the node from another tree"
                )
            node = node.parent
        return DecLockRefResult(delta=delta)

    def supports_prefix_sharing(self) -> bool:
        return not self.disable

    def evictable_size(self):
        return self.evictable_size_

    def protected_size(self):
        # protected size refers to the size of the cache that is locked
        return self.protected_size_

    def all_values_flatten(self):
        values = []

        def _dfs_helper(node: TreeNode):
            for _, child in node.children.items():
                values.append(child.value)
                _dfs_helper(child)

        _dfs_helper(self.root_node)
        return torch.cat(values)

    ##### Internal Helper Functions #####

    def path_device_indices(self, node: TreeNode) -> torch.Tensor:
        values = []
        while node is not self.root_node:
            values.append(node.value)
            node = node.parent
        if not values:
            return self._empty_device_indices
        values.reverse()
        return torch.cat(values)

    def _match_prefix_helper(self, node: TreeNode, key: RadixKey):
        access_time = time.monotonic()
        node.last_access_time = access_time

        child_key = key.child_key(self.page_size)

        value = []
        while len(key) > 0 and child_key in node.children.keys():
            child = node.children[child_key]
            child.last_access_time = access_time
            prefix_len = child.key.match(key, page_size=self.page_size)
            if prefix_len < len(child.key):
                new_node = self._split_node(child.key, child, prefix_len)
                value.append(new_node.value)
                node = new_node
                break
            else:
                value.append(child.value)
                node = child
                key = key[prefix_len:]

                if len(key):
                    child_key = key.child_key(self.page_size)

        return value, node

    def _split_node(self, key: RadixKey, child: TreeNode, split_len: int):
        # new_node -> child
        # New node inherits child's priority (represents shared prefix)
        new_node = TreeNode(priority=child.priority)
        new_node.hit_count = child.hit_count
        new_node.children = {key[split_len:].child_key(self.page_size): child}
        new_node.parent = child.parent
        new_node.lock_ref = child.lock_ref
        new_node.key = child.key[:split_len]
        new_node.value = child.value[:split_len].clone()
        child.parent = new_node
        child.key = child.key[split_len:]
        child.value = child.value[split_len:].clone()
        new_node.parent.children[key.child_key(self.page_size)] = new_node

        # Split hash_value if it was already computed, otherwise leave as None
        new_node.hash_value, child.hash_value = split_node_hash_value(
            child.hash_value, split_len, self.page_size
        )
        new_node.event_hash_value, child.event_hash_value = split_node_hash_value(
            child.event_hash_value, split_len, self.page_size
        )

        return new_node

    def _inc_hit_count(self, node: TreeNode):
        node.hit_count += 1

    def _insert_helper(
        self,
        node: TreeNode,
        key: RadixKey,
        value,
        priority: int = 0,
        inserted_len: int = 0,
    ):
        # Convert None priority to 0
        if priority is None:
            priority = 0
        access_time = time.monotonic()
        node.last_access_time = access_time
        # Update priority along the path (take max to propagate higher priority)
        node.priority = max(node.priority, priority)
        if len(key) == 0:
            return 0, node

        child_key = key.child_key(self.page_size)

        total_prefix_length = 0
        while len(key) > 0 and child_key in node.children.keys():
            node = node.children[child_key]
            node.last_access_time = access_time
            prefix_len = node.key.match(key, page_size=self.page_size)
            total_prefix_length += prefix_len
            key = key[prefix_len:]
            value = value[prefix_len:]

            if prefix_len < len(node.key):
                new_node = self._split_node(node.key, node, prefix_len)
                new_node.priority = max(new_node.priority, priority)
                node = new_node
            else:
                node.priority = max(node.priority, priority)
            # Nodes this request already inserted were counted back then.
            if total_prefix_length > inserted_len:
                self._inc_hit_count(node)
            if len(key):
                child_key = key.child_key(self.page_size)

        if len(key):
            new_node = TreeNode(priority=priority)
            new_node.parent = node
            new_node.key = key
            new_node.value = value.clone()
            if total_prefix_length + len(key) > inserted_len:
                self._inc_hit_count(new_node)
            node.children[child_key] = new_node
            self.evictable_size_ += len(key)
            self._update_leaf_status(node)
            self._update_leaf_status(new_node)
            # Hash will be computed lazily during event emission
            self.kv_events.record_store(new_node)
            node = new_node
        return total_prefix_length, node

    def _print_helper(self, node: TreeNode, indent: int):
        """Prints the radix tree in a human-readable format."""
        stack = [(node, indent)]
        while stack:
            current_node, current_indent = stack.pop()
            print(
                " " * current_indent,
                len(current_node.key),
                current_node.key.token_ids[:10],
                f"r={current_node.lock_ref}",
            )
            for key, child in current_node.children.items():
                stack.append((child, current_indent + 2))

                assert key == child.key.child_key(self.page_size), (
                    f"{key=}, {child.key.child_key(self.page_size)=}"
                )

    def _delete_leaf(self, node):
        key = node.key.child_key(self.page_size)
        v = node.parent.children.pop(key, None)
        assert v == node, f"parent does not have child key, {key}"

        self.evictable_size_ -= len(node.key)
        if node in self.evictable_leaves:
            self.evictable_leaves.remove(node)
        self._update_leaf_status(node.parent)

    def _update_leaf_status(self, node: TreeNode):
        if node.evicted or node.lock_ref > 0:
            if node in self.evictable_leaves:
                self.evictable_leaves.remove(node)
            return

        for child in node.children.values():
            if not child.evicted:
                if node in self.evictable_leaves:
                    self.evictable_leaves.remove(node)
                return

        if node not in self.evictable_leaves:
            self.evictable_leaves.add(node)

    def _total_size_helper(self):
        total_size = 0
        stack = [self.root_node]
        while stack:
            current_node = stack.pop()
            total_size += len(current_node.value)
            for child in current_node.children.values():
                if child.evicted:
                    continue
                stack.append(child)
        return total_size
